feedback: If a learner gives only water and expects the plant to thrive in the dark, point to the pale, leggy growth: water alone is not enough; the plant also needs light.
If a learner tries to give the plant a food bowl, note that a plant in the light grows without one because it makes its own food using light — only the animal needs feeding.
When a learner restores a missing need and the plant recovers, name it: 'You found the need — without light it went pale; back in the light, its new leaves turn green and it grows stronger.'
Reinforce that changing one thing at a time (e.g. only the light) shows clearly what caused the change.
activities.intendedInsight: A need is proven by its consequence: withhold it and the living thing visibly suffers. Plants and animals need different things — plants need light and make their own food, animals cannot make food and must be fed.
learnerActions: Set up (or run a model of) two living things to care for: a bean plant in a pot and a small animal such as a hamster in a hutch.

Choose what to provide to each from a shared set of supplies: a watering can, a lamp for light, air, warmth, and a food bowl. With a real hamster, always give it everything it needs; only leave needs out in the model.
Give the plant water but leave it in the dark, and watch over time (days, or time-compressed in a model) to see it stay alive but grow pale and leggy.
Notice that the plant has NO food bowl and still grows, while the animal must be fed — then explain why the two lists differ.
Rescue a wilting or pale plant by restoring the one missing need, and describe what changed.
activities.title: Side-by-side windowsill care bench

feedback: If a learner names only a healthy state, prompt: 'What if this one were missing — what would you see?'
If a learner lists animal needs for the plant (e.g. a food bowl), revisit that the plant makes its own food from light and does not eat.
Confirm correct need–part pairings and have the learner say the matching consequence.
activities.intendedInsight: Each need is linked to a part or behaviour of the organism and to a specific consequence if it is missing.
learnerActions: Look at a plant and an animal and name each basic need aloud: for the plant — water, light, air, suitable temperature; for the animal — water, food, air, shelter/warmth.
Pair each need with the part or behaviour that uses it, e.g. roots take up water, leaves use light, the animal's mouth takes in food.
For each need, say what the living thing would look like if that need were missing (e.g. 'no water → wilts', 'no light → pale', 'no food → weak').
activities.title: Name the needs and what uses them
